assumptions: The Program emits 1-TM-score constraints; raw TM-score is recovered as 1 minus the stored score.
Adenylate kinase is a representative example in the paper, but this collection is one target-level protocol slice rather than the full 86-protein benchmark.

The 50 full variants preserve the paper's draw allocation for the required Boltz-2 target slice: ten beta settings times five seeds times five diffusion samples equals 250 models. The generated query-only inputs diverge from the paper's matched-depth MSA protocol.
The paper reports five seeds but not their values; implementation seeds 0 through 4, query-only backend inputs, beta values, and proposal order are paired identically across full and fused arms.
Only backends explicitly registered through register_reviewed_pair_scaling_backend may execute; absence raises an error instead of silently running beta zero.

Both smoke and full generated variants require only query-only Boltz-2. This removes private AlphaFold 3 parameters and a user-held AlphaFold Server MSA from the execution gate, at the cost of unknown and potentially material accuracy loss relative to the paper.

Each full variant scores all five fixed-sequence proposals in one optimizer batch; the backend folds the sequence once with five diffusion samples and returns every sample instead of retaining only model zero. The smoke variant remains one proposal and one diffusion sample.
unknowns: The required Boltz-2 2.2.1 backend uses an audited Pairformer pre-hook and rejects a run unless scaling fires once per trunk pass; it never substitutes an unscaled model. The optional AlphaFold 3 backend applies the same fail-closed policy.

A closer paper-fidelity recipe is available only by explicitly setting use_msa=true with max_msa_seqs=1024 and supplying the exact user-held AlphaFold Server alignment through PROTOFUSE_AF3_SERVER_MSA_A3M. Adding AlphaFold 3 also requires explicitly requesting models=("alphafold3", "boltz2"). Neither recipe is part of generated-program review or smoke.
Official AlphaFold 3 parameters are licensed, privately mounted runtime data and are never committed or redistributed. They are optional for this collection's runnable benchmark.
The collection encodes one adenylate-kinase protocol slice, not the complete 86-target benchmark.
Per-state Cα RMSD success, worst-case RMSD, best-minimum TM-score, and fill ratio remain ensemble-level collection analysis beyond the per-model TM-score constraints.

Every per-model and per-state TM-score remains in constraint metadata, but a Proto Program candidate has one structure slot, so later structure-producing constraints overwrite earlier coordinates and the retained candidate carries only the final Boltz-2 structure. Paper-level coordinate and Cα RMSD ensemble analysis therefore requires separately archived backend outputs and cannot be reconstructed from the candidate structure field alone.

Because every proposal in this collection has the same protein sequence, the sweep validates the pair-scaling hook, batching/cache behavior, fail-closed execution, and paired throughput. It is not sufficient by itself to measure learned-surrogate ProtoFuse accuracy. A meaningful learned-fusion evaluation requires varied proposals or independent trajectories with held-out full-model labels.
